text:
Jamal (customer): Hey team — hitting a 413 when calling POST /v1/rerank. Body is ~2.4MB, but I'm not sure if it's the number of docs or the query length. Response body just says \"Request Entity Too Large\". Request ID: req_abc123. Happening in prod, blocking a customer.

Maya (Support): Thanks Jamal — can you paste a minimal repro (curl or sample payload) and the exact response body/headers? 413 could be gateway or app-level.

Jamal (customer): Here's a sanitized curl we used (trimmed docs but same shape):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-***\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{
    "query": "<a ~15k char user query...>",
    "documents": ["doc1... ~2k chars", "doc2... ~2k chars", ..., "doc120... ~2k chars"]
  }'
```

Response: HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 15:23:45 GMT
Content-Type: application/json

Body: `{ \"error\": \"Request entity too large\" }`

No other headers indicating which limit triggered this. Customer expects a clearer error so they can auto-fallback.

Maya (Support): Got it. Two quick asks for triage: 1) full raw response headers (if available), 2) a tiny sample payload that still reproduces the 413 (so eng can run locally). In the meantime, can you try reducing docs to 50 or truncating the query to 2k chars to see if it passes?

Jamal (customer): I tried dropping to 60 docs — still 413. Dropped to 40 docs + query trimmed to ~2k chars and it succeeded. So looks like a combination of total payload size + maybe token count. Customer wants deterministic guidance (what thresholds to enforce client-side).

Maya (Support): Ok thanks — escalating to engineering. @Alex (Eng) can you take a look? Links: request id req_abc123, sample curl above.

Alex (Eng): Looking. Quick context: rerank currently has multiple gating layers: 1) HTTP gateway max body (10MB limit), 2) service-side validators that enforce per-doc char cap and a combined token limit (tokenization via shared tokenizer). Gateway 413 comes from the layer that rejects raw body > 10MB. We return 422 when tokenization fails/limits exceeded deeper in the pipeline, and 413 if the HTTP body is too big for the gateway.

Alex (Eng): From the sample it sounds gateway 413 is the culprit here — 120 docs * ~2k chars -> ~240k chars + query 15k chars = ~255k chars (~0.25MB) which is below gateway limit, so odd. Can you attach the exact raw payload length? The request id shows several retries and a proxy adding headers; there may be base64 attachments inflating size.

InfraBot: [automated log] proxy-01: client req req_abc123 received, content-length: 256512, forwarded to rerank-svc-2, svc returned 413 at 15:23:45, gateway-throttle: false, token-limit-check: not-reached.

Alex (Eng): Thanks infra log — content-length 256512 (~250KB). That's well below the 10MB gateway limit. That means some intermediate component returns 413 when per-field or validation rules fail (we recently rolled out a per-request doc-count cap defaulted at 100 for older tenants, 50 for new). I think the tenant in question has a policy of max_docs=50 enforced by a filter; when exceeded we currently map that to a generic 413 instead of a structured 4xx with details.

Maya (Support): Ah — that explains why reducing to 40 docs works. Can you confirm whether the enforcement is per-tenant and whether the error has anything in headers? Customer reported none.

Alex (Eng): Confirmed: enforcement is per-tenant and stored in the tenant config service. It returns an internal error code (ERR_DOC_COUNT_EXCEEDED) which our gateway was mapping to 413 without passing the code/body through. That's on us. We'll fix mapping and make the body include {\"error\":\"doc_count_exceeded\", \"limit\":\"50\"} plus a docs link.

Riley (Product): Noted — this is a UX gap. We should: a) standardize rerank error responses to include which limit tripped (doc_count, total_tokens, per_doc_chars), b) add headers like X-Redwood-Limit and X-Redwood-Limit-Value, and c) update docs with a clear client-side validation snippet. Short-term: Support should provide a template message telling customers to cap docs and truncate queries.

Priya (Billing): Also flagging: the customer was auto-scaling and we saw a sudden spike in billable tokens when they retried. We'll coordinate a grace note while this is being fixed.

Alex (Eng): Proposed plan: I will open a small PR to change error mapping (map ERR_DOC_COUNT_EXCEEDED -> 400 with structured JSON) and add the tenant limit value. ETA: 2 business days for a patch to the gateway and 1 week for docs. Will add regression tests.

Maya (Support): Thanks. I'll reply back to the customer with a short workaround + ask to confirm exact counts so we can verify once fix is live. Template I used:

```
Hi — thanks for the report. Temporary workaround: reduce number of documents to <=50 or batch your docs into multiple rerank calls, and shorten queries to <=2000 chars. We're working to make the error clearer (will include which limit you hit). Can you also send the full request-id header if it occurs again?
```
Jamal (customer): Tried the <=50 docs approach — success. Customer is happy with a workaround but wants clearer error for automation. Appreciate the quick escalation.

Riley (Product): I'll add a small docs snippet and create a help center article that maps common rerank errors to actions (e.g., cut docs, shorten query, batch). I'll also add a short item to the console's per-route SLO page to show configured max_docs for the tenant.

Alex (Eng): Filed ENG-7492 with the mapping change, test cases, and a small telemetry event to surface which limit triggered. Assigning to me.

Maya (Support): Closing loop: Jamal, will re-open iff you see anything after the patch. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Jamal (customer): Thanks all — saved the client.
